post.caption: Bolo ties are official in three states. Arizona went first, naming it official neckwear in 1971. New Mexico and Texas both made it their state tie in 2007. The name probably comes from the bola, a South American cowboy rope. Legend says a silversmith wore his hatband as a tie while riding. Earlier still, Native men tied a silver concha at the neck. Hopi and Navajo silversmiths have made bolo slides in silver. Slides are usually silver, most often set with turquoise. Slid up to the collar, it dresses up like a necktie. Wyoming's legislative dress code says bolo ties shall be permitted.
